schema_version: v0 — skill-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: Birth a node — a new track or an aside. Unpack it into WHAT (the intent) and HOW (the approach), and trace it up to the Telos.
why: The work loop's entry. Nothing enters the system unarticulated (Law 5: intent and implementation share an address). The trace-to-Telos step enforces the charter's own rule — 'what can't trace up doesn't belong' — at the cheapest possible moment, before any cost is spent (Law 1: the resolver is spent on the novel).
state: v0 — first cast 2026-07-15. Behavior is a resolver-occupied question nexus; the role-replacement staircase applies (this occupancy is measured out, never declared out).
produces: a node in intention fill-state — WHAT/HOW unpacked, traced, not yet cast. Casting (type it, bind its gates) happens later, inside /sorted.

nexus.note: SKILL.md carries the live question set; this is the charter-face record of it.
nexus.routes_forward: /sorted (resolution pivot) — /challenge fires INSIDE this skill as a required step (ticket challenge-fires-at-intent, 2026-08-03), no longer a route out of it
nexus.routes_back: cannot trace to Telos → it doesn't belong; say so and stop, don't file it

input_contract.from_idea: WHICH captured idea this intention came from — an id under CairnCommons/ideas/, a path to one, or 'none, because <X>' with a JUDGEABLE reason (one carrying a resolvable referent). Added 2026-08-04 with skill:/idea, closing a measured red: the trace pointed only UP, to a Law, and never BACK — so the moment one idea bore three intentions, the three could not say they were siblings and none could point at the prose that bore them. It cites the COMMONS record and never a berth path: a berth is instance-space and means nothing on another machine. Judged by skills/intent/door.py, so the edge exists rather than being claimed.
input_contract.what: the intent in one sentence — the AIM, not the approach. A firing that cannot say what it is for is the confabulation CP1 forbids; refusing here is cheaper than refusing at any later gate.
input_contract.how: the approach, first-cut only. Forced because an intent with no imaginable approach is usually two intents, or none — and /sorted deconstructs what this names.
input_contract.traces_to: which Telos aim or Law this traces up to — or, explicitly, that NOTHING traces. This is the routes-back edge and the whole reason the gate is cheap: an intention that shouldn't exist dies on this field.
input_contract.shape: new track or aside — so the tree stays honest about what is being opened versus what is being noted in passing.
input_contract.falsifier: what would tell us this is done, or tell us it was the wrong intent. First-cut horizon; /sorted refines it. Law 3 as a required field: an unmeasured claim is labeled a hypothesis at birth, not later.
input_contract.challenge: the adversarial pass's five answers (better_approach, prior_art, hidden_assumption, real_collision, back_up), forced at every birth — ticket challenge-fires-at-intent, 2026-08-03. The event is the one that already fires (a node being born), never a clock; as an optional route this pass fired zero times while one measured session re-derived already-solved work three times. Required at BOTH exits: a kill that never stood the pass is an unexamined kill. The floor is presence — hollow answers are the ticket horizon's re-open, recorded verbatim by the trace and standing at Akien's gate.
input_contract.exit: routed_forward or routed_out. Forced because the kill is the exit that vanishes into conversation today, and an unnamed exit is how it goes on vanishing.
input_contract.bullets: the exit-time finding — a list of {text, stratum} with stratum in code|tree, standing at Akien's gate. Forced at BOTH exits: a routed_out firing with no bullets is a node killed with no record of why.

how_it_learns: By downstream rejection: when a node keeps dying at a LATER gate that /intent should have caught (a bad trace, a missing shape), that miss becomes a gate-record and /intent's question set gains a question. It learns which questions actually route work. AS OF 2026-08-01 the interim-by-hand half is over on the RECORDING side: /intent is the first skill to fire inside the Learning Block anatomy (ticket intent-becomes-a-learning-block), so every firing is traced with its consumer, greens included, and every exit emits a stratum-tagged finding that stands at Akien's gate until an approve or disprove names it. What is NOT yet built is the back-edge this field describes: nothing yet connects a LATER gate's rejection to the /intent firing that let it through. The firing is now recordable; the downstream-rejection collector is a separate node and is named as absent rather than implied.
traces_to: Law 5 (intent and implementation share an address)
owner: the skills charter gates writes to this file; Akien ratifies changes (signature gate)
the_door: skills/intent/door.py — the semantic half the flat {field: why} shape cannot express, on the sorted-door template with zero seam change. It judges TWO things this charter already DECLARED and nothing enforced: that `from_idea` RESOLVES, and that `challenge` carries all five answers. The second is not a new rule — this charter's own challenge field says 'the floor is presence', and a one-key object satisfied check_input and therefore satisfied nothing. Quality of an answer stays the model's and stands at Akien's gate; EXISTENCE of a referent and PRESENCE of the five are floors, and floors are physics (Law 4).
proof: a skill node reaches done only when cairnmap recompiles green (the skill class's derivation gate). IOU until cairnmap is built — tracked in proofs/.
provenance: converged in the founding design conversation (MAP.md 'Workflow + starting skills', 2026-07-15); first exemplar of the skill-charter mold.
